newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil recovers, tone weak.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil recovers, tone weak.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil swaps recovered slightly late afternoon on Thursday tracking firmer crude values but current bearish sentiment still undermine prices, brokers and traders said on Friday.
June and July gas oil swaps were quoted at $24.50/$24.60 up from its morning quotes at $24.30/$24.50 per barrel and $24.40/$24.55.
IPE Brent futures recovered from its previous day's losses. up 13 cents at $18.45 at 0440 gmt.
Traders said unsold prompt gas oil supplies were flooding the market. They said few buyers are likely to emerge later today to take away some lengths.
"There were only two buyers in the market yesterday," said on trader.
They also said that there were eight physical offers from five sellers on Thursday, evident that the market is weak.
They added that arbitrage cargoes from the West threatened to push prices lower while regional demand remained thin.
Up to four 60,000 to 80,000 tonnes tankers from the Mediterranean and Black Sea is expected to head to Asia for arrival in early July.
Brokers said June jet/gas oil regrade was little changed from its morning quotes at -0.40/-0.50 cents.
July was quoted at 0.10/0.20 cents, 10 cents lower from its morning levels.
Traders attributed the softer regrade quotes to lower physical jet fuel prices. Jet fuel traded lower at $24.05.
Fuel oil swaps were also indicated lower. Brokers attributed the overall bearish sentiment in the swaps market to overnight crude losses.
June swaps was quoted at $100.00/$100.75 down from Thursday's $100.50/$101.25. July was quoted at $99.00/$99.50
